figure: FIGURE 7.5 (KV cache size vs context, by attention geometry)
issue: The upper-right annotation cluster is illegible: the two annotation sentences ('9.5K FP16 bound reaches the 436 GB budget at ~166K' and 'vs GQA FP16 (2.62 → 0.33 MB/tok)') plus the '8×' marker are stacked in the same region and overlap the 640 GB dotted reference line, the 436 GB dash-dot reference line, and the red (full-MHA FP16) / orange (full-MHA FP8) data lines, which at 100K–200K context sit at ~262–524 GB, i.e. exactly through that text. Text glyphs cross lines and the lines cross text, so the reader cannot cleanly read the annotations or trace the curves there.
evidence: Rendered page 152: in the top-right, the horizontal dotted line (8×H100 raw, 640 GB) and dash-dot line (KV budget ~436 GB) run straight through the multi-line annotation text; the red and orange curves terminate in the same band. The annotation lines are vertically packed with no clear gap, and the '8×' label sits between them. All underlying numbers recompute correctly (436,000 MB / 2.62 MB/tok ≈ 166K; 2.62/0.33 ≈ 8; 9,500 × 2.62 MB ≈ 24.9 GB; 128,000 × 2.62 MB ≈ 335 GB; 436,000 / 0.33 ≈ 1.32M), so this is a composition/legibility defect, not an arithmetic one.
acceptance_test: Reposition the upper-right annotations (and the '8×' marker if it is duplicated there) into a whitespace region (e.g. the open area between the 10 and 1000 gridlines above the curves, or a callout box in the right margin) so that no annotation glyph intersects the 640 GB dotted line, the 436 GB dash-dot line, or the red/orange data lines, and so the two annotation sentences are not stacked on top of each other. Re-render at 150 dpi and confirm every annotation line is fully legible without crossing another element, and that the '8×' ratio is shown only once (at the 9.5K vertical marker) unless a second, clearly separated callout is intended.
